If you already follow Nick, you know what to expect: sharp takes, market chaos, founder brain, and the occasional banger you’ll see clipped on the timeline five minutes later.

Episodes will be streaming live on YouTube, so make sure you’re subscribed to catch the next one as it happens.

**[Subscribe to Choose Rich Live!](https://www.youtube.com/@chooserichnick/streams)**

Avalanche, and Chainlink to its Schwab Crypto platform in the

million brokerage account holders. The firm manages $13 trillion
in client assets and charges 0.75% per crypto trade.

----------
**Welcome back!** An AI that had only ever studied recordings of brain surgery got its first live patient, and he can see again. Anthropic taught Claude to run lab equipment, 116 rivals signed one cyber warning, and ChatGPT's temporary chats learned to remember you.

**In today's Generative AI Newsletter:**

* **Surgeons:** How did AI save a man's eyesight?

* **Anthropic:** What equipment can Claude now run?

* **Big Tech:** Why did 116 companies sign the same warning?

* **ChatGPT:** What do temporary chats now remember?


----------







----------
## The first AI brain surgery worked

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/e3c5c7d3-3170-47ce-a159-00d434f371b7/Aug_28_-_1.jpg?t=1787906451)
Caption: 

Rhys Hibbert, 48, [was going blind](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/aug/27/london-neurosurgeons-ai-assisted-operation-brain-tumour). An 11mm tumor sat on his pituitary gland, in a spot where a millimeter mistake means blindness, stroke or death.

His surgeons at London's National Hospital for Neurology and Neurosurgery brought in help that had never touched a live patient. An AI, trained at UCL on hundreds of surgical videos, watched the camera feed and colored the danger in real time, this is a nerve, that's a vessel, cut neither.

It was the first AI-assisted brain tumor removal ever. It happened in May, and the hospital sat on the news until Thursday while he recovered.

He walked out without glasses within a week. He says he sees like he's got a 360-degree panoramic view.
